issues.description: The solution declares the screen buffer symbol as 'screen_buffer' but the code (both in set_pixel and main) references 'display_start'. The problem statement and template expect the symbol 'display_start'. This name mismatch leads to undefined symbol references and will prevent the solution from assembling/compiling, causing confusion for students who expect to use 'display_start'.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the buffer symbol consistent. Either declare 'display_start' in the solution (replace 'screen_buffer' with 'display_start') or update all references in the solution to use 'screen_buffer'. Ensure the name matches the template and the problem statement so the code assembles and students can follow the intended API.

issues.description: The conceptual entity 'start of the screen/framebuffer' is referred to as display_start in the problem statement and the template, but the solution's .bss declares it as screen_buffer. This inconsistent identifier naming for the same memory buffer creates a mapping problem: students expect and are instructed to use display_start, but the solution's declaration uses a different name, increasing cognitive load and risking confusion or errors when comparing template, problem text, and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent identifier for the framebuffer across all artifacts. Rename the solution's 'screen_buffer' label to 'display_start' (or, alternatively, rename the template/problem references to 'screen_buffer') and update all references accordingly so problem_statement.md, pixel.asm (template), and pixel.asm (solution) use the same name.
